text.p: German pharmaceutical wholesaler Andreae-Noris Zahn AG (Anzag) said on Wednesday it plans to pay another attractive dividend on 1996/1997 earnings, after a sharp hike in the 1995/1996 payout.

In the text of a speech to be delivered to shareholders, chief executive Hermann Franke said such a payout would only be possible through "consistent and fast action" in the face of further state cutbacks in the health sector, which were likely to cause stagnant, or even lower sales.
"Sales in the first half of the current year did not match the level of the previous year," Franke added. Sales fell two percent to 2.1 billion marks, he said.
However he said the pharmaceutical market was still a growth market from a medium-term perspective.
Anzag upped its dividend for 1995/1996 to 18 marks from 14 marks after posting a 19 percent rise in net profit to 38.5 million marks.
